input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN running against us: before engaging another provider we must disclose to Vendor, and match for Vendor, any more favourable commercial offer we receive. This is the wrong direction (the rule only welcomes MFN pricing in Customer's favour) and it is unbounded — no defined product or service line, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred position reached by deleting the obligation; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere that needs preserving.

proposal.summary: Delete the most-favoured-nation / matching obligation imposed on Customer in Section 7.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this most-favoured-nation obligation: our playbook does not accept an open-ended duty to disclose third-party offers or match them for Vendor, and it contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. If Vendor wants pricing protection, we can discuss an MFN in our favour instead.
